guideTitle: 6 Best Door Knob Grips for Arthritis in 2026
metaTitle: Best Door Knob Grips for Arthritis in 2026
metaDescription: Six silicone door knob grips marketed for arthritic or weak hands, compared on grip surface, knob fit, pack count and extras. A daily-living aid guide.
introParagraphs: Turning a round knob needs a pinch, a squeeze and a twist all at once, which is exactly the combination that stiff or sore hands find hard. Grip covers are marketed to people with arthritis or limited hand strength because they add friction and a softer, wider surface. They are a daily-living aid, not a treatment, and nothing in this guide implies a medical benefit. The practical question is how much easier a given cover makes it to turn a knob with a flat palm or a loose hand.

We evaluated six covers from Enjoy Cover, Eggone and Able Life on grip force, handle size, one-handed use, stated fit and pack count. Based on product specs and buyer feedback, four are Enjoy Cover designs, one is the six-piece Eggone set with glow inserts, and one is the Able Life EZ cover that is positioned as a cheaper alternative to a lever replacement.

Each pick notes what the listing says and what it leaves out, including sizes that are not stated. The tables then map situations such as a wall-hitting door, a dark hallway or a whole-house set to a named pick, with a reminder to measure your own knobs first.

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Maximum Grip Silicone Door Knob Grips
specs: Marketed as a senior living aid
products.description:
This Enjoy Cover two-pack is the most direct grip upgrade here, made from 100 percent silicone that the listing says is nontoxic, BPA free and allergy free. The maker markets it as an arthritis and senior living aid and describes the surface as soft, nonslip and comfortable. It fits most standard popular sizes in a single size.

The benefit is a simple sleeve that increases friction so a loose or tired hand can turn the knob without a hard pinch. The tradeoff is that one size has to cover many knobs, and the listing gives no diameter range, so measure your knob and compare before buying. It also adds no wall protection or night visibility.

Installation takes seconds and cleaning is soap and water. Next to the upgraded Enjoy Cover, this version emphasizes the material and the maximum-grip surface. Compared with the Eggone, you get fewer pieces but a clearer safety statement. Choose it as the default if you want a plain, well-described grip. Because the same maker also sells the upgraded and Doorstop versions, this is the baseline the others are measured against: if the plain cover turns your knob easily, the extras are optional.
products.bestFor: A plain, soft silicone grip for one door, on both sides.
cons: No diameter range in the listing

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Upgraded Ergonomic Door Knob Grips
products.description:
The upgraded Enjoy Cover is a two-pack of nonslip silicone grips with a shape the listing calls ergonomic. It says they make knobs easier to grasp and turn for people with limited hand strength or dexterity, and that they stretch to accommodate different knob sizes while keeping a snug fit.

The benefit is a shaped surface from a maker that focuses on this need. The tradeoff is that the listing does not give the dimensions of the grip, so check the product page for how large the contact area is. A stretch fit may also loosen over time on a worn knob.

Setup is slip-over with no tools or modifications. Compared with the original Maximum Grip two-pack, the upgraded design emphasizes shape over material claims. Next to the Eggone's ribbed surface, the Enjoy Cover relies on a smooth ergonomic form. Choose it if you want the maker's shaped version. Because the listing mentions stretching to accommodate different knob sizes, a very large or very small knob is the case to test first.
products.bestFor: People who want a shaped grip surface on a standard round knob.
cons: Stretch fit may loosen with wear

products.name: Eggone 6 Pcs Silicone Door Knob Grips with Glow Inserts
products.description:
Eggone sells six ribbed silicone grips, each about 3 inches wide and 2 inches deep. The listing says the ribbed texture is comfortable on older hands and fingers and that the glow inserts help in the dark. It is made of silica gel described as chemically stable and durable.

The benefit is a whole-house set with a gripping ribbed surface and a visible knob in a dark hall. The tradeoff is that the 3 by 2 inch size is specific, so check it against your knob, and the listing does not describe how firmly it stays on.

The ribs give fingers something to catch, which a smooth cover does not. Compared with the Enjoy Cover two-packs, the Eggone is the only one with glow inserts and the only one that states a size. Choose it if you have several doors and want a textured, visible grip. The anti-static note in the listing also means less spark from a metal knob in dry weather, a small but real comfort when you touch several doors a day.
products.bestFor: A whole-home set with a ribbed surface and night visibility.
cons: Size may not suit very large knobs

products.name: Enjoy Cover Doorstop Silicone Door Handle Grip
products.description:
The Enjoy Cover Doorstop combines a nonslip grip with a soft silicone bumper that stops the knob from hitting the wall. The listing calls it an all-in-one cover with an ergonomic design, markets it for arthritis and seniors and says the soft bumper prevents wall damage.

The benefit is one product that handles both grip and wall protection, which removes a separate floor doorstop from a walkway. The tradeoff is added bulk, so it may feel larger in the hand than a plain sleeve, and the listing gives no diameter range.

It installs by slipping over the knob. Compared with the plain two-pack, the bumper is the difference. Next to the Eggone, it targets the wall rather than night visibility. Choose it for a door that swings hard into a wall. Its listing gives the same ergonomic claim as the other Enjoy Cover versions, so the choice comes down to whether the wall bumper is worth the added size.
products.bestFor: A door that bangs the wall and a hand that needs a better grip.
pros: Removes the need for a floor stop

products.name: Enjoy Cover Decorative Door Knob Cover Grips

specList.label: Fit
specList.value: Standard popular sizes including Ball, Cove, Tylo

products.description:
This Enjoy Cover version adds decorative styling, with the listing saying colors will become available so you can personalize a room. It is nonslip, static free and said to feel less cold and less hot than a bare metal knob.

The listing names the standard knob styles it fits, including Ball, Cove and Tylo, which is the most specific fit statement among the Enjoy Cover versions. The tradeoff is that the listing is only partly clear about the color options and size, so check the product page. It also lacks a bumper or ribs.

Installation is slip-over with no tools, and cleaning is with soap and water. Compared with the plain Maximum Grip two-pack, this adds the static-free and temperature notes. Choose it if you want a grip that blends with room decor. The less-cold, less-hot note is about comfort when the knob sits in winter drafts or summer sun, and the static-free claim is shared with the Eggone's anti-static note. Because colors are described as coming soon, confirm what is available on the product page.
products.bestFor: A decorative grip for standard Ball, Cove or Tylo style knobs.
pros: Less cold and less hot than bare metal

products.name: Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips
products.description:
Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips are non-slip silicone covers that stretch over a door knob. The listing says they help open doors effortlessly and that they cost less than replacing a knob with a lever.

The benefit is avoiding a hardware change, which matters for renters. The tradeoff is that the listing is brief and gives no size or texture detail, so confirm fit on the product page. It does not list extras.

Installation is a simple stretch-over. Compared with the Enjoy Cover versions, Able Life shares fewer specs. Choose it if you want a basic cover. With its listing leaving size and texture unstated, it is the pick where measuring your knob before ordering matters most. Its one clear claim, lower cost than a lever, is worth weighing against the more detailed Enjoy Cover listings.
products.bestFor: Renters who cannot swap the door hardware.
pros: Positioned as lower cost than a lever

buyingCriteria.explanation: A wider, softer surface lets the palm do the turning when finger strength is limited. The Eggone is about 3 inches wide, and the Enjoy Cover versions are described as soft nonslip silicone. Pick a cover that fills your palm rather than a thin sleeve. Always try turning with a flat hand. Hard-edged or thin sleeves can dig into the palm, so softness matters as much as width. The Doorstop's bumper adds bulk at the back, which can make the grip larger but also heavier.

A loose cover spins on the knob and the latch does not move. Most listings say one size fits most standard round knobs, but give no number, so measure first. The Enjoy Cover Decorative names Ball, Cove and Tylo types, and the Eggone states 3 x 2 inches. Wrap a string around the knob and compare. The Enjoy Cover Maximum Grip and the Upgraded versions both state stretch or one-size fit rather than a diameter, which is why the string test is the safest approach.

Friction is what reduces the squeeze needed. The Eggone has ribs that the listing says suit older hands, while the Enjoy Cover Maximum Grip has a soft nonslip surface. Silicone also stays slightly tacky for damp hands. Avoid hard plastic covers. A tacky surface can reduce the squeeze needed to keep a hand from slipping, though it does not change the latch resistance. The Enjoy Cover Decorative adds a static-free surface, which helps with tiny shocks but not with friction.

You should be able to open the door with one hand while carrying something. A palm push on a wide cover works better than a pinch. The upgraded Enjoy Cover is shaped for limited strength. Test with a flat palm before buying a set. Compare how the Eggone at 3 inches wide and the Doorstop with its bumper each sit against your palm. A cover that fits the shape of your hand is easier to turn with the heel of the hand.

A door that hits the wall causes dents and noise. The Enjoy Cover Doorstop adds a soft bumper. The Eggone adds glow inserts for a dark hallway. Choose extras only if you need them. The Decorative cover adds styling rather than a mechanical extra. Because the Doorstop's bumper compresses against the wall, leave a few inches of swing room behind the door.

Knobs are touched constantly, so covers should wash easily. Silicone cleans with soap and water, and the Enjoy Cover lists nontoxic, BPA free silicone. The Eggone is silica gel described as chemically stable. Remove and dry covers regularly. Plan to wash covers monthly in a busy household. A cover that traps grime against the knob can become slick again.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip and texture
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated the surface each listing describes. Eggone's ribs and the Enjoy Cover's soft silicone lead, and Able Life gives the least detail. None of the listings gives a friction measurement, so this is a relative judgment from descriptions and buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs, we compared fit statements. Eggone states 3 x 2 inches, the Decorative names Ball, Cove and Tylo, and others say most standard sizes. The Able Life listing gives no fit range, which is why it carries the measure-first note.

howWeEvaluated.title: One-handed use
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged how easy each looks to turn with a palm or weak grip, from grip force and handle size, with no medical claims. A wide soft surface scored higher than a thin sleeve because a flat palm needs less finger closure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: The Doorstop's bumper, the Eggone's glow inserts and the Decorative's static-free surface were counted as extras. The Doorstop leads on wall protection, and the Eggone leads on night visibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value per door
howWeEvaluated.description: Pack count was compared. Eggone gives six and the Enjoy Cover two-packs give two. The Eggone's six covers cost less per door than a two-pack.

faq.q: Do grip covers help with arthritis?
faq.a: They add friction and a wider surface, so the knob can be easier to turn with a loose hand. They are daily-living aids, not treatments, and do not claim medical benefit. If you have pain, talk to a professional about options. A cover adds grip, but it will not change how stiff the latch is.

faq.q: Will one size fit my knob?
faq.a: Most listings say one size fits most standard round knobs. The Eggone states about 3 x 2 inches. Measure your knob and check the product page. A cover that spins on the knob is a sign the size is wrong.

faq.q: Which cover is best for a door that hits the wall?
faq.a: The Enjoy Cover Doorstop has a soft bumper that stops the knob from hitting the wall. It is also a grip. Check swing room first. Leave a few inches of swing room behind the door for the bumper to work.

faq.q: Are ribs better than smooth silicone?
faq.a: Ribs give fingers something to catch, as on the Eggone. Smooth soft silicone suits palm pushing. Try both if you can. Many people keep a ribbed cover on the bathroom door, where hands are damp, and a smooth one elsewhere.

faq.q: Should I choose a lever instead?
faq.a: Levers usually need less hand closure but require a hardware change. A cover is cheaper and needs no tools. Able Life positions its cover as a lower cost alternative. A lever is also a larger change that a renter may not be allowed to make.

faq.q: How do I keep covers clean?
faq.a: Wash silicone with soap and water and dry it fully. The Enjoy Cover lists nontoxic, BPA free silicone. Avoid harsh solvents. Check the cover monthly for tears, since a worn cover grips less.

faq.q: Can I use a grip cover on a lever or oval knob?
faq.a: These covers are described for round knobs, and the Decorative version names Ball, Cove and Tylo shapes. An oval or egg-shaped knob may not seat evenly, and a lever needs a different product. Check the knob shape on the product page before ordering.
